newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania opposition blasts pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: Albania opposition blasts pyramid schemes.

text.p: An Albanian opposition party on Tuesday sharply condemned get-rich-quick schemes that have mushroomed across Albania and accused the government of President Sali Berisha of abusing the schemes for its benefit.

In a strongly-worded statement, the centre-right Democratic Alliance Party (DAP) said Berisha's ruling Democratic Party had misused money invested by ordinary Albanians in pyramid schemes to finance its campaign for reelection in a general election last May.

"DAP observes that the collapse of such pyramid schemes has started...the government and the one-party state of the Democratic Party should bear responsibility for the losses incurred by Albanians," the party said in a statement.
Nobody at the Democratic Party's headquarters was immediately available for comment.

Get-rich-quick money schemes promising returns of up to 50 percent a month have been proliferating in Albania for several years and have drawn hundreds of millions of dollars, sending alarm bells ringing at the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
In a move for transparency, parliament set up a committee to investigate such schemes.

The DAP, set up by a group of dissidents who fell out with the ruling Democrats soon after they came to power in a landslide victory over the Socialist Party in March 1992, said the pyramid schemes were destined for collapse and slammed the accumulation of vast sums of money outside the banking system.
